headline: High-risk shared filesystem and unsandboxed server-side code make Langflow→plano interactions prone to leakage, conflicts, and cascading errors.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Langflow can read/write the server filesystem and run unsandboxed Python code; plano exposes config files and OpenAI-compatible API inputs. If Langflow outputs are copied into plano configs or prompts, attacker-controlled content can steer downstream behavior. The bridge is plausible but not automatic, so medium fits better than high.
conditions: IF Langflow flow outputs are pasted into plano prompts or config.yaml without sanitization
IF plano treats file or prompt content as instructions rather than data
mitigations: Add a fixed delimiter and instruction/data separation in the handoff
Review any Langflow-generated text before copying into plano
Disable automatic ingestion of file contents into prompts
Use a short allowlist for fields passed between systems

B_data_leakage.rationale: Langflow touches flow inputs, intermediate outputs, and server filesystem files; plano touches logs, traces, metrics, and config.yaml. A shared workspace or copied artifacts could move sensitive flow data into plano telemetry or API payloads. No direct shared filesystem is documented, so this is medium rather than high.
conditions: IF both agents are deployed on the same host or shared workspace
IF Langflow outputs are forwarded into plano logs, traces, or API requests
mitigations: Store each agent in separate directories
Redact secrets before exporting logs or traces
Turn off verbose logging for both systems
Audit config.yaml and flow exports for embedded credentials

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Langflow has broad network egress, shell, subprocess, and filesystem write; plano also has broad network egress and can read config files. If they share a mutable workspace or server-side state, concurrent writes and overlapping external calls can race or overwrite each other. The profiles show no locking, so the conflict risk is high.
conditions: IF Langflow and plano share the same writable directory or config store
IF both are allowed to mutate shared artifacts during the same run
mitigations: Place each agent in a separate filesystem namespace
Serialize writes to shared artifacts with a lock file
Disable concurrent runs against the same workspace
Use read-only mounts for shared inputs

D_cascading_error.rationale: Langflow is a workflow orchestrator that can chain agents and tools; plano is an AI gateway/proxy with OpenAI-compatible chat completions. If plano consumes Langflow-produced outputs as authoritative prompts or routing data, errors can propagate into downstream actions without verification. That default handoff is dangerous enough to rate high.
conditions: IF plano routes or executes based on Langflow-generated text without validation
IF Langflow-produced facts are treated as authoritative by plano
mitigations: Insert a validation step between Langflow and plano
Require schema checks on all exchanged payloads
Log provenance for every handoff
Block direct action-taking on unverified model output

E_compliance.rationale: Langflow stores per-flow component credentials and handles flow inputs/intermediate outputs, while plano handles logs, traces, metrics, and config.yaml. If regulated data is routed through both, retention and residency controls can diverge. No specific certifications are listed for either, so the mismatch is plausible but not proven.
conditions: IF regulated data is present in Langflow flows and also appears in plano logs or traces
IF retention or deletion requirements differ between the two systems
mitigations: Classify data before sending it to either system
Set matching retention windows where possible
Purge logs and traces on a fixed schedule
Avoid storing secrets in flow inputs or config.yaml
